fields.h1: Build Recruiting Landing Pages That Turn Visitors Into Applicants
fields.hero_description: Build recruiting landing pages that screen applicants, book interviews, and save every application to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Recruiting Page
fields.features_subheading: A recruiting landing page sells one role or program to candidates and takes the application on the same page.
fields.feature_1:
A page written from the job description

Paste the job description and the pay into a prompt. Emergent builds the page with its application form and the table behind it, then changes any section when you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
Screening questions that route applicants

Ask the questions that decide a fit, such as a required license or a night shift. Applicants who answer yes reach the hiring manager, and every other application stays on file.
fields.feature_3:
Interview slots candidates book themselves

Set the interview length and the hours. The page shows only open slots, drops each one as soon as it is booked, and the app emails every candidate a reminder before the interview.
fields.feature_4:
Applications in a database you own

Each application lands in a database you own as one row of answers. Through an API, the app can also send every application to the applicant tracking system recruiters use now.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts to the recruiter who owns the role

Name a recruiter for each role and choose Slack or email for the alert. Referrals and qualified applicants reach that person, and a reminder follows if nobody opens them.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and the code if you want it

Publish the page on the company's own domain, which is included and uses credits. On paid plans, the full code exports to your GitHub repository for an engineer to extend later.

fields.usecase_heading: Recruiting Pages for Four Hiring Moments
fields.tab_content_1:
Two yes answers put an applicant in front of the manager

Fairbourne Freight is hiring a night warehouse lead at $24 an hour. The page asks 2 screening questions: a forklift certification, and the 10 PM to 6 AM shift. Celestine Odhiambo answers yes to both, and hiring manager Bram Ostrowski gets her application by email. It saves to the applicants table with her answers.
fields.tab_content_2:
12 Saturday interviews, booked by candidates

Hollingbrook Grocers fills its Saturday hiring day with 15-minute interviews from 9 AM to noon, 12 slots in all. Each candidate picks a time, and a booked slot leaves the page. Hugo Vandersloot takes 10:30 AM, one of the last 3 open slots, and the app emails him a reminder on Friday.
fields.tab_content_3:
One QR code at the fair builds the internship list

Bexley Pike Robotics brings a QR code to its career fair table. Students scan it and join the summer internship list with their major and graduation year, and 48 sign up before the fair closes. Recruiter Wen Calderwood gets an email digest of the new signups at 8 AM the next day.
fields.tab_content_4:
Referrals arrive with the referring employee named

Omar Hollis works as a hygienist at Juniper Quay Dental and refers Saskia Thorvaldsen for an open hygienist role. The form saves her name and resume link to the referrals table, with Omar listed as the referrer. Recruiter Tobias Delacroix-Ruiz gets a Slack message with both names.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Recruiting Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps take recruiting landing pages from one open role to a published page that screens and saves every applicant.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the role and the one action
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Lead with what a candidate weighs
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 List the answers that decide a fit
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the page in a prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose one role, or one program such as a summer internship, and one action for the candidate: apply or book an interview. A page that asks for two things splits attention. Settle the action before writing any copy.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put the pay, the schedule, and the location in the opening lines, then 2 or 3 reasons to take the job. Keep the company history to one sentence. The role is what the candidate came to read, and the details decide whether they keep going.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write down the answers that rule an applicant in, such as a forklift license or a night shift. These become the screening questions, and everything else waits for the interview. Keep the form short enough to finish on a phone in a few minutes.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste the pitch and the screening questions into Emergent, and say what happens on submit: who gets the email and which table keeps the application. Emergent builds the page and the database behind its form. Prompt again to change any section.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Name where each applicant goes next: the hiring manager's inbox, a Slack message for referrals, or the applicant tracking system through its API. The app sends every application there and keeps its own copy in the database you own, with each answer.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Apply as a candidate on a phone
fields.howto_step_6_des: Open the page on a phone and submit two test applications. Make the first pass the screening questions, and make the second fail one. Check that only the first reaches the hiring manager, and that both rows land in the table with every answer filled in.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Go live on the company's domain, then share the page in the job board posting and as a QR code at events. Read the first day's applications in the table and fix any question candidates skip.

faq_plan.a: Recruiting landing pages are single web pages that ask candidates for one action on one role or program, such as an application or an interview booking. Each one carries one pitch, the pay and schedule, and a short form, and every response lands in one table.

faq_plan.q: How do I create recruiting landing pages?
faq_plan.a: Describe the role and its screening questions, and say what should happen when someone applies. Emergent's AI landing page builder turns that prompt into a working page with its form and database. Send two test applications from your phone before sharing the link. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What should a recruitment landing page include besides the role description?
faq_plan.a: Beyond the role description, include the pay range, a short application form, and a line on what happens after someone applies. Say when applicants will hear back and how many interviews follow. Use a real photo of the workplace or team instead of stock images, and name a person candidates can contact.

faq_plan.q: What should I look for in recruitment landing page examples?
faq_plan.a: Look for pages that ask for one action and show the pay before the form. Check what each page shows after the form is sent, because that confirmation tells candidates what happens next.

faq_plan.q: How is a job landing page different from a job board listing?
faq_plan.a: A job landing page is a page the employer owns and designs for one role, while a job board listing follows the board's layout and sits next to other employers' openings. On your own page you choose the screening questions and where applications are stored. In a page built with Emergent, every application lives in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Do I need a career landing page if my company already has a careers site?
faq_plan.a: Not always. A career landing page helps when one role or event needs its own pitch and form, such as a hiring day or an internship drive. Keep the careers site as the directory of every opening, and point ads and QR codes at the landing page, where those candidates see one action.

faq_plan.q: How do I track which job board sent each applicant to my recruiting landing page?
faq_plan.a: Give every place you post the role its own link with a source tag, such as ?source=fair, and have the form save that tag with each application. The applicants table then shows where every candidate came from. Judge each source by hires, not visits, as you would a sales funnel landing page, and drop the ones that bring traffic but no hires.

faq_plan.q: Can recruiting landing pages send applications to an applicant tracking system?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the applicant tracking system has an API. Apps built with Emergent connect to any tool with an API and sync data in and out. Each application can then reach the tracking system as it arrives, with a copy kept in the page's own table. Ask the system's admin for API access first, and map every form field to its field there.

faq_plan.q: Can a recruiting landing page show up in search results for job listings?
faq_plan.a: Yes, it can become eligible. Google says adding JobPosting structured data makes job postings eligible to appear in a special user experience in Google Search results. It also says you must include the required properties for your content to be eligible for display in the job experience. Add that markup to each role's page and test it before the role goes live.

faq_plan.q: Should recruiting landing pages cover one open role each, or several?
faq_plan.a: Give each role its own page when roles differ in pay, schedule, or screening questions, because one form cannot ask the right questions for each. Roles that match on all three can share a page with a role picker. A hiring push with one deadline across several roles works like a campaign landing page. With Emergent, each new page is one more plain-English prompt.

plan.angle: The top 10 for recruiting landing pages is example galleries and landing-page builders: they show screenshots of finished pages and stop there. This page shows four recruiting pages built from a prompt and follows each applicant to where they land: an open role whose two screening questions decide who reaches the hiring manager, a Saturday hiring day with capped interview slots, a career fair QR code that adds students to an internship list, and an employee referral page that keeps the employee who sent each candidate. The FAQ covers the definition, what a recruitment landing page needs, examples, job board listings, careers sites, source tracking, ATS hand-off, job search results and one page per role.
